basis: All 40 rows of the DPS planning register v0.1, reviewed alongside the SC/DPS integration plan and the cited interfaces. This is a proposed collaboration view; no row is approved here for detector operation.

level_clarification.title: Collaboration clarification, 8 September 2026: required LAr coverage is a prerequisite for HV availability and voltage setting

integration.title: SC/DPS software integration plan, interaction matrix and power-loss example

pds.title: PDS interface, EDMS 3309688/1, section 5 (contains disputed optical rules)

dcs.title: The ProtoDUNE Single Phase Detector Control System (2019)

dss.title: The CERN Detector Safety System for the LHC Experiments

work.title: Site access, work-control and laser-safety requirements: exact references still needed

teams.name: Cryogenics
teams.headline: HV stays unavailable until LAr covers all required instrumentation, including the cathode.
teams.share: The measured LAr level and whether it is reliably above the required minimum; relevant cryogenic faults and changes that affect data quality.
teams.agree: The minimum level and reference point that guarantee the required coverage; measurement reliability; the response to a falling level; and restart checks.

teams.name: High voltage and field cage
teams.headline: Keep voltage-setting, enabling and ramping unavailable until the required LAr level is established.
teams.share: Requested and measured states, ramping, faults, affected detector region, and the reason for a shutdown.
teams.agree: The approved startup and shutdown sequence, linked field-cage outputs, and the still-open response of other systems to a cathode trip.

teams.name: TPC electronics and APA/CRP teams
teams.headline: Agree which combinations of detector states are allowed.
teams.share: Actual APA/CRP bias and electronics states, readiness, cooling problems, and the detector region affected.
teams.agree: Allowed states during filling and tests; response to cathode or mains-power loss; and which fan, heater or condensation problems need a shutdown.

teams.name: Photon detection system (PDS)
teams.headline: Take turns with camera lights and external lasers; keep running during purity measurements.
teams.share: The exact PDS state that excludes external light, the region affected, equipment faults, and readiness to resume.
teams.agree: Light-off confirmation and settling time; purity-monitor data labels; equipment protection limits; and the conflicting wording in the old PDS interface.

teams.name: Cameras and illumination
teams.headline: Check with PDS before turning on camera lights.
teams.share: Whether illumination is actually on or off, which lights are involved, and where their light can reach.
teams.agree: How the second request is blocked, how light-off is confirmed, and what to do if light appears unexpectedly. The rule concerns illumination; camera power alone is not a proven conflict.

teams.name: Lasers, calibration and movable devices
teams.headline: Name the source and its purpose before applying a light rule.
teams.share: External-laser emission and shutter state, PDS calibration activity, or device position and movement.
teams.agree: The affected region, PDS handoff, laser-safety checks, permitted movement and the calibration record needed by analysis.

teams.name: Purity monitors
teams.headline: Publish when and where a purity measurement affects PDS data.
teams.share: Actual start and stop times, affected region, and whether the activity record is reliable.
teams.agree: Timing precision, the affected PDS channels and any settling time. Arrange a quiet interval only when a measurement needs one.

teams.name: Rack power, cooling and electrical services
teams.headline: Protect the affected equipment and explain what lost power.
teams.share: Rack or supply faults, cooling and power availability, the loads affected, and the state of protection equipment.
teams.agree: Which loads switch off, which essential loads may stay on, response time, power-loss ordering and inspection before restart.

teams.name: Data acquisition, timing and data quality
teams.headline: Know whether a run may start and which data need a label.
teams.share: Run type, timing readiness, configuration identity, the detector region in use and the recorded activity intervals.
teams.agree: When to stop, pause or continue a run; who can change settings; how analysis receives quality information; and fresh configuration after recovery.

teams.name: Installation, integration and run coordination
teams.headline: Make it clear who is using each part of the detector.
teams.share: Active work, the named test owner, affected area, agreed exceptions and the handback to operations.
teams.agree: The work and test procedure for each stage, exception expiry, escalation and the checks before returning to a run.

teams.name: Detector Protection System (DPS) and Slow Controls
teams.headline: Make the agreed action happen and show a useful reason.
teams.share: Protection availability, blocked requests, actual equipment state, faults and the steps still needed for restart.
teams.agree: A named subsystem owner, the affected equipment, the required response time and a test of each action. Keep required protection working through the failures it must handle.

rules.title: People are working in an affected area
rules.why: Protect people from the hazardous equipment in that work area.
rules.action: Apply the site's approved access and isolation procedure before work or energization.
rules.restart: The authorized work-control role releases the area and the required equipment checks are repeated.
rules.open: Name the exact site procedure, work boundary and responsible role.
rules.installation: Verify isolation before work.
rules.commissioning: Check both access permission and the approved test plan.
rules.run: Use the approved operations access procedure.

rules.title: A hazardous laser is requested or its access checks fail
rules.why: Protect people near the laser and its beam path.
rules.action: The laser-safety system allows or stops emission according to its approved design, regardless of PDS or run state.
rules.restart: The authorized laser-safety role confirms the conditions for restart.
rules.open: Identify the laser, access zone, protective devices and restart procedure.
rules.installation: Use the approved laser installation procedure.
rules.commissioning: Test the laser-safety checks before emission.
rules.run: Keep the laser-safety system active during calibration.

rules.title: HV is unavailable until LAr is above the required minimum
rules.why: The liquid argon must cover all required detector instrumentation, including the cathode, before cathode HV is available for operation.
rules.action: Keep voltage-setting, enabling and ramping blocked until a reliable measured LAr level is above the specified minimum. This is a standing prerequisite, independent of whether anyone requests HV. Monitoring and protective shutdown remain available.
rules.restart: A confirmed level above the minimum satisfies this prerequisite; the other HV checks must also pass. HV starts only through a deliberate command. A falling level while HV is on follows the separate protection rule P-002.
rules.open: Specify the minimum level, its reference point and coverage margin, the affected instrumentation, and which reliable measurements establish it. The requirement for coverage before HV availability is fixed; these details remain to be supplied.
rules.installation: Keep cathode HV connected to the cryostat isolated and unavailable while the required LAr coverage is absent.
rules.commissioning: Keep voltage-setting, enabling and ramping blocked until the measured level is reliably above the minimum; a test request does not waive this prerequisite.
rules.run: Allow HV commands only after this level requirement and the other HV checks pass. Reaching the level does not automatically switch HV on.

rules.title: Liquid-argon level reaches the HV protection limit
rules.why: Loss of the required coverage creates an HV equipment-protection concern.
rules.action: Shut down the affected cathode HV through the agreed protection system and notify the affected teams.
rules.restart: Investigate the level change; confirm safe conditions; deliberately restart through the approved sequence.
rules.open: Confirm the reference geometry, threshold, response time and affected HV supply. A prototype number is not a universal detector limit.
rules.installation: Check the level-to-HV protection connection.
rules.commissioning: Test the low-level shutdown at the approved scope.
rules.run: Keep the low-level protection active while HV is on.

rules.title: A relief valve opens or an agreed boiling-risk condition occurs
rules.why: These cryogenic conditions can make energized HV unsafe for equipment.
rules.action: Shut down the affected cathode HV for the conditions listed in the approved cryogenics/HV rule.
rules.restart: Cryogenics and HV investigate, confirm recovery and authorize a deliberate restart.
rules.open: List the qualifying conditions, signals, response times and shutdown scope.
rules.installation: Identify and check the relevant cryogenic inputs.
rules.commissioning: Test each agreed cryogenic shutdown condition.
rules.run: Keep the agreed cryogenic protection active.

rules.title: Cathode HV has an abnormal current excursion
rules.why: An electrical fault may require rapid HV protection.
rules.action: Apply the approved HV shutdown rule, prevent an immediate restart and tell PDS and DAQ what happened.
rules.restart: Keep the fault record; have the HV expert investigate and follow the approved recovery sequence.
rules.open: Approve the current limit and duration for each operating state, the response time and linked outputs.
rules.installation: Establish test limits and the affected supply.
rules.commissioning: Test the shutdown and retain the current record.
rules.run: Apply the approved automatic HV protection.

rules.title: Cathode HV shuts down: linked field-cage outputs follow
rules.why: The HVS interface specifies this coordinated shutdown to avoid incorrect HV current readings. That reason alone does not establish equipment damage.
rules.action: Shut down the associated field-cage termination supplies as specified by the HVS interface.
rules.restart: Check both measured states and use the approved restoration order.
rules.open: Confirm the linked channels and timing. Review the register's equipment-damage label against the stated source rationale.
rules.installation: Check which field-cage supplies belong to each cathode.
rules.commissioning: Test the coordinated shutdown and the return sequence.
rules.run: Apply the agreed linked shutdown when cathode HV stops.

rules.title: A fire alarm affects HV or detector power
rules.why: Protect people and equipment under the facility's fire response.
rules.action: Apply the approved fire response. The HVS interface calls for all HVS supplies off, including cathode and CRP/field-cage/APA bias.
rules.restart: Wait for the facility's release and the equipment owners' recovery checks.
rules.open: Agree detector-wide power zones, any essential loads and the full response beyond HVS.
rules.installation: Map the fire response to the installed equipment.
rules.commissioning: Test the approved fire-to-power actions.
rules.run: Apply the approved facility and HVS fire response.

rules.title: Smoke is detected in a rack
rules.why: Smoke may indicate a damaging rack fault or fire.
rules.action: The rack protection shuts down the agreed loads and identifies the affected rack.
rules.restart: Inspect the rack and follow the authorized reset; power does not return just because the alarm clears.
rules.open: Confirm the production design, loads, essential exceptions and response time.
rules.installation: Check the sensor and the loads it protects.
rules.commissioning: Test smoke detection and the actual power response.
rules.run: Keep rack protection available and report the shutdown cause.

rules.title: Water is detected in a rack
rules.why: Water can damage energized equipment.
rules.action: Remove power from the loads specified by the rack's approved leak-protection rule.
rules.restart: Inspect the leak and equipment before an authorized restart.
rules.open: Agree sensor locations, affected loads, timing and inspection criteria.
rules.installation: Check leak-sensor placement and power connections.
rules.commissioning: Test detection and the affected power outputs.
rules.run: Keep the approved leak protection active.

rules.title: A rack overheats or loses required cooling
rules.why: Equipment may exceed its safe temperature.
rules.action: Apply the agreed rack or device response: shut down the affected loads when the protection condition is reached.
rules.restart: Restore cooling, inspect as required and confirm temperatures before restart.
rules.open: Set limits and delays for the actual equipment; identify any essential loads allowed to remain powered.
rules.installation: Check cooling and temperature monitoring.
rules.commissioning: Test cooling loss and overtemperature response.
rules.run: Protect loads using their agreed limits.

rules.title: A rack protection sensor or controller fails
rules.why: Equipment must not silently lose a protection function it relies on.
rules.action: Show the failed protection clearly and apply the response agreed for that particular failure.
rules.restart: Repair and test the protection before returning affected equipment to its approved operating state.
rules.open: Specify which failures stop running loads. Losing a monitoring display is not automatically the same as losing local protection.
rules.installation: Identify failure indications and check connections.
rules.commissioning: Disconnect or simulate each relevant failed input.
rules.run: Use the approved response for the failed protection path.

rules.title: A PDS supply exceeds an agreed electrical limit
rules.why: Abnormal current or voltage can damage PDS equipment.
rules.action: The approved protection switches off the affected supply or output group and confirms the resulting state.
rules.restart: PDS investigates, clears the cause and authorizes the required checks before restart.
rules.open: Specify limits, duration, output grouping and reset conditions for each supply.
rules.installation: Check supply-to-channel connections and limits.
rules.commissioning: Test the electrical fault response and readback.
rules.run: Apply the agreed PDS supply protection.

rules.title: PDS power, readout or calibration equipment overheats
rules.why: Temperature can threaten PDS equipment, including power-over-fiber hardware.
rules.action: Apply the device's agreed automatic protective action and report which equipment is affected.
rules.restart: Restore the cooling or repair the fault; confirm the device's recovery conditions.
rules.open: Identify sensors, limits, affected outputs and recovery for each device.
rules.installation: Check the installed sensors and cooling.
rules.commissioning: Test each device's overtemperature response.
rules.run: Keep device protection active during physics and calibration.

rules.title: TPC electronics has a fan, heater or condensation problem
rules.why: The consequences differ between loss of cooling, heater faults and condensation.
rules.action: Use the response agreed for the particular problem. The available interface does not yet choose every alarm or shutdown action.
rules.restart: The electronics owner confirms the problem is resolved and the appropriate checks pass.
rules.open: Decide separately which conditions need attention and which must switch off equipment, with limits and timing.
rules.installation: Check fans, heaters and environmental measurements.
rules.commissioning: Establish the response for each type of fault.
rules.run: Apply the agreed device-specific actions.

rules.title: Mains power is lost while anode bias and electronics are on
rules.why: If one must switch off before the other, that order must remain possible during the power failure.
rules.action: The required order is still a question for the electrical and detector owners. Do not claim that a software command alone guarantees it.
rules.restart: Follow the approved recovery after power returns and check the actual equipment states.
rules.open: Establish whether an order is required; then measure how long the electronics remains supported and how long bias removal takes.
rules.installation: Record power connections and any backup supplies.
rules.commissioning: Measure the behavior during a representative power-loss test.
rules.run: Use only the power-loss behavior that owners have accepted.

rules.title: Cold electronics is requested during filling or a warm test
rules.why: The allowed temperature and immersion conditions have not been established for every electronics system.
rules.action: Follow an owner-approved test or operating procedure. The matrix does not grant a new permission or impose one universal shutdown rule.
rules.restart: Confirm the allowed environment and the electronics checks for that procedure.
rules.open: List the permitted warm, gas, liquid, filling and draining conditions for each relevant device.
rules.installation: Use the approved checkout conditions.
rules.commissioning: Review each intended cryogenic test state.
rules.run: Use the electronics' approved operating conditions.

rules.title: The grounding monitor reports a problem
rules.why: A warning about grounding may affect noise, equipment or both; the action depends on the actual condition.
rules.action: Alert the electrical/grounding expert and apply the approved response for the reported problem.
rules.restart: The responsible owner investigates and confirms the conditions for return.
rules.open: Distinguish noise warnings from damaging faults and decide which equipment, if any, must stop.
rules.installation: Check grounding and monitor installation.
rules.commissioning: Classify warnings and test the agreed responses.
rules.run: Use the agreed escalation and protection rules.

rules.title: A required protection signal becomes unreliable
rules.why: A missing or unreliable reading cannot serve as confirmation that a protected condition is satisfied.
rules.action: Apply the agreed response for that protection signal and show what is missing. The response of equipment already on must be defined per rule.
rules.restart: Repair the signal path and verify its operation before releasing the affected restriction.
rules.open: Agree which signal failures block startup or stop equipment, and the acceptable detection time.
rules.installation: Check sensor identity, connections and fault indication.
rules.commissioning: Test missing, delayed and contradictory protection inputs.
rules.run: Keep protection failures visible and follow their agreed response.

rules.title: Camera illumination and PDS are requested together
rules.why: These activities must take turns in the affected optical region.
rules.action: Block the second request. If light appears unexpectedly, switch off or block the light where possible, alert operations and mark the affected data.
rules.restart: Confirm illumination is actually off and allow the agreed settling time before PDS resumes.
rules.open: Define the excluded PDS state and affected region. Reconcile the old interface's bias-off wording; a damage-based PDS trip is not established by the historical exclusion alone.
rules.installation: Record ownership of any light and PDS test.
rules.commissioning: Test both request orders and the light-off handback.
rules.run: Keep camera illumination and the agreed PDS state from overlapping.

rules.title: An external laser and PDS are requested together
rules.why: Ionisation or alignment laser activity must take turns with PDS in the affected region.
rules.action: Block the second request. Keep the laser's personnel-safety checks in force independently.
rules.restart: Confirm emission is off and the shutter is in its approved closed state before PDS returns; record any accidental overlap.
rules.open: Define the excluded PDS state, optical region, confirmation signals and settling time.
rules.installation: Coordinate laser work with PDS tests.
rules.commissioning: Test both request orders and the laser handback.
rules.run: Keep external-laser emission and the agreed PDS state from overlapping.

rules.title: A purity monitor operates while PDS records data
rules.why: The overlap reduces PDS measurement quality; it does not require PDS bias removal in this draft.
rules.action: Keep PDS running. Record the affected time and detector region so analysis can identify those data.
rules.restart: No PDS restart is required for this overlap. Record when the effect ends; arrange quiet intervals when scientifically useful.
rules.open: Agree timing precision, affected channels and settling time. Correct the old PDS interface text that requires bias off.
rules.installation: Label any affected engineering data.
rules.commissioning: Allow and record deliberate overlap.
rules.run: Allow overlap and mark affected data; PDS bias stays on.

rules.title: PDS uses its own calibration light
rules.why: This light is intentional and must be identifiable in the data.
rules.action: Use the agreed PDS/DAQ calibration sequence and record the pulse settings, time and affected region.
rules.restart: End calibration and confirm the agreed return to ordinary data taking.
rules.open: Agree allowed run types, recorded information and settling time.
rules.installation: Use the agreed calibration checkout.
rules.commissioning: Record the test configuration and light pulses.
rules.run: Use a declared calibration activity and label its data.

rules.title: Power-over-fiber supplies the applicable vertical-drift PDS
rules.why: These PDS channels need power-over-fiber to operate.
rules.action: Allow the required power-over-fiber source while PDS is active, with its own equipment and applicable laser-safety protection.
rules.restart: Follow the PDS power and protection checks for the affected channels.
rules.open: Identify the supplied channels, protection limits and recovery. Keep this source distinct from an external calibration laser.
rules.installation: Check the power-over-fiber connections and protection.
rules.commissioning: Test the dependency and device protection.
rules.run: Keep the required power source available to its PDS channels.

rules.title: A light source has no agreed classification
rules.why: Its effect on PDS and its allowed use are unknown.
rules.action: Hold the new conflicting activity until the source and PDS owners agree how it may be used.
rules.restart: Name the light source, its purpose and its affected region, then follow the agreed rule.
rules.open: Complete the light-source list; distinguish camera light, external laser, PDS calibration and power-over-fiber.
rules.installation: Identify each installed light source.
rules.commissioning: Review a new source before testing it with other systems.
rules.run: Allow only activities covered by an agreed rule.

rules.title: HV changes during data taking
rules.why: A ramp, trip or recovery changes the conditions represented by the data.
rules.action: Record the HV state and affected interval; stop, pause or continue according to the agreed run plan.
rules.restart: Confirm the required stable conditions before returning to the intended physics run.
rules.open: Agree acceptable physics conditions and the run response. HV equipment protection is handled by the separate protection rules.
rules.installation: Label any HV test data.
rules.commissioning: Record before-and-after states around a ramp.
rules.run: Apply the agreed run response and mark affected data.

rules.title: Cryogenic conditions change within equipment-safe limits
rules.why: Pressure, temperature, purity or circulation changes can affect the interpretation of data.
rules.action: Record the agreed indicators and affected interval so data quality can be assessed.
rules.restart: Record when the conditions again meet the agreed physics criteria.
rules.open: Set data-quality criteria separately from equipment-protection limits.
rules.installation: Record relevant conditions during tests.
rules.commissioning: Study and label the effects of cryogenic changes.
rules.run: Mark affected data according to the agreed physics criteria.

rules.title: Timing is not ready for the requested run
rules.why: The requested synchronized data taking may not work correctly.
rules.action: Block a new step that needs the missing timing. If timing fails during a run, follow the agreed run response and mark affected data.
rules.restart: Restore and verify timing, then follow the agreed reconfiguration procedure.
rules.open: Agree the timing-ready definition and the in-run stop, pause or continue policy.
rules.installation: Check timing connections and device identity.
rules.commissioning: Test loss and restoration of timing.
rules.run: Require the timing needed by the selected run type.

rules.title: A control connection or service is lost
rules.why: Commands may no longer reach equipment and displayed values may be old.
rules.action: Block commands that cannot be verified and show the unknown state. Required equipment protection must survive the failures specified for it.
rules.restart: Read the actual equipment state after reconnection; do not replay old power commands automatically.
rules.open: Agree how long each reading remains usable and what an ongoing run should do.
rules.installation: Identify the connections needed for each test.
rules.commissioning: Test connection loss and reconnection.
rules.run: Show unknown states and follow the agreed run response.

rules.title: Two people or systems request conflicting changes
rules.why: Equipment should not receive competing instructions.
rules.action: Accept changes only from the agreed owner for that setting and activity; report why another request was refused.
rules.restart: Resolve who owns the task and confirm the actual settings before proceeding.
rules.open: Name the owner for each type of setting and the expert-work handover. Seeing a value does not grant permission to change it.
rules.installation: Name the person in charge of each checkout.
rules.commissioning: Test conflicting requests and explicit handover.
rules.run: Use the agreed ownership of power, protection and run settings.

rules.title: A calibration or instrumentation device needs to move
rules.why: Allowed motion depends on detector state, position and the particular device.
rules.action: Use the device's approved movement procedure and hold requests outside it.
rules.restart: Confirm the actual position and the checks needed before other detector activities resume.
rules.open: List the devices, allowed positions, HV conditions and any credible damage mechanism.
rules.installation: Record the installed device and movement limits.
rules.commissioning: Test movement only in the approved detector conditions.
rules.run: Use the agreed movement and return procedure.

rules.title: Experts are using a detector region needed by a new run
rules.why: A new run could interrupt an active test or overwrite its settings.
rules.action: Hold the new run or configuration until the test owner hands the region back, or run coordination agrees a controlled transition.
rules.restart: Record who has finished, which equipment is ready and who now has control.
rules.open: Agree how reservations, expiry and handback are recorded.
rules.installation: Name the work owner and affected area.
rules.commissioning: Make each test reservation visible.
rules.run: Check ownership before starting or reconfiguring a run.

rules.title: ProtoDUNE shifters followed a manual HV-current recovery
rules.why: This records what operators did in one historical configuration.
rules.action: Use the old sequence as evidence for discussion. Each proposed shutdown or data-taking step needs its own present-day justification.
rules.restart: Use the currently approved procedure for the detector concerned.
rules.open: Determine which historical steps protected equipment and which coordinated data taking; do not copy the sequence as a universal DUNE rule.
rules.installation: No additional operating permission follows from this history.
rules.commissioning: Use the history to identify questions and tests.
rules.run: Follow the approved current recovery procedure.

rules.title: A temporary protection exception is active
rules.why: The detector is not in its ordinary approved operating configuration.
rules.action: Show the affected rule, equipment, responsible person and expiry; hold normal operation unless the approved exception permits it.
rules.restart: Remove the exception and complete the required checks before ordinary operation resumes.
rules.open: Specify which exceptions are allowed and who may approve them. Existing non-bypassable safety functions remain in force.
rules.installation: Keep exceptions within approved work control.
rules.commissioning: Record the test scope, owner, expiry and restoration checks.
rules.run: Keep any approved exception visible to operations.

rules.title: We cannot identify which equipment a signal or command affects
rules.why: An action could reach the wrong channel, rack or detector region.
rules.action: Hold new activation until the connection is verified. An active protection fault follows its pre-agreed conservative response.
rules.restart: Correct and verify the equipment mapping before releasing the restriction.
rules.open: Agree the installed-equipment record and the response when that record is missing or inconsistent.
rules.installation: Record and verify installed connections.
rules.commissioning: Test signals and commands against the actual equipment.
rules.run: Require a verified mapping for the requested activity.

rules.title: The cause of a protective shutdown has cleared
rules.why: The equipment and run configuration still need to be checked before use.
rules.action: Have the responsible owner inspect and reset the affected system, confirm actual states and request a deliberate restart.
rules.restart: DAQ applies and checks the required configuration before operations resumes the intended run.
rules.open: Name who may reset each rule and the required inspection, sequence and run checks.
rules.installation: Recheck the work and isolation conditions.
rules.commissioning: Test recovery as well as the original fault.
rules.run: Confirm recovery and fresh configuration before resuming.

rules.title: An APA, CRP or field-cage supply exceeds its safe limits
rules.why: An electrical or thermal fault can damage the equipment served by that supply.
rules.action: Switch off the affected output or the group approved by the owners, and check the measured result.
rules.restart: Investigate the fault and follow the approved supply and detector recovery checks.
rules.open: Agree limits, shared output groups, response time and any required linked actions.
rules.installation: Verify supply-to-detector connections and protection settings.
rules.commissioning: Test the affected output and any approved linked group.
rules.run: Use the agreed supply protection and recovery.

rules.title: Cathode HV is lost while other detector systems remain on
rules.why: The required response of APA/CRP bias, TPC electronics and affected PDS is not established by one universal rule.
rules.action: Record actual states, notify experts and hold new unapproved transitions. Apply only the protective actions already approved for that detector configuration.
rules.restart: Owners confirm the allowed combination of states and the recovery sequence.
rules.open: Resolve horizontal-drift and vertical-drift cases separately, including relevant PDS power arrangements, damage mechanism, timing and shutdown order.
rules.installation: Identify the independent supplies and affected connections.
rules.commissioning: Study the proposed linked actions in approved tests.
rules.run: Use approved actions; an open row grants no new operating permission.

rules.title: A requested HV or APA/CRP state differs from the agreed run or test
rules.why: A valid commissioning combination may be unsuitable for the intended physics run.
rules.action: Follow the agreed sequence for that detector and activity. Hold a new transition that is not covered by the procedure.
rules.restart: Have the relevant owners reconcile the measured states before declaring the detector ready for that run.
rules.open: Approve the combinations, ordering and stability checks for each stage and detector type.
rules.installation: Use the approved checkout sequence.
rules.commissioning: Use a named test plan and record each state change.
rules.run: Require the combination of states agreed for the selected run.

rules.title: Cathode, APA, CRP or field-cage settings change the data conditions
rules.why: Analysis needs to know which detector configuration produced the data.
rules.action: Record measured settings and the time and region affected. Pause or continue according to the run plan; data quality alone does not demand a hardware trip.
rules.restart: Record the return to the intended stable configuration.
rules.open: Agree physics ranges, stability time and the boundary between runs or data intervals. Coordinate this row with the HV-specific row Q-003.
rules.installation: Label the test settings in engineering data.
rules.commissioning: Record data before and after each approved change.
rules.run: Mark any departure from the configuration agreed for the run.
